subject: maths
title: Place Value: 4-Digit Numbers, 1,000 More or Less and Counting Through Zero
seo_title: Year 4 Place Value Worksheets: 4-Digit Numbers, Counting in Multiples and Negative Numbers
standard_text: Count in multiples of 6, 7, 9, 25 and 1,000; find 1,000 more or less than a given number; count backwards through zero to include negative numbers; recognise the place value of each digit in a four-digit number (thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones); order and compare numbers beyond 1,000; identify, represent and estimate numbers using different representations.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 place value maths worksheets for the National Curriculum: the value of each digit in 4-digit numbers, partitioning, place value counters, 1,000 more or less, counting in 6s, 7s, 9s, 25s and 1,000s, comparing and ordering, and counting back through zero. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: In a 4-digit number each digit is worth thousands, hundreds, tens or ones. The place decides the value.
key_sub: The 3 in 4,352 is worth 300. Write 0 in any empty place, change only the thousands digit for 1,000 more or less, and remember to say 0 when you count back past it.
body_html:
Thousands, hundreds, tens and ones

A 4-digit number has a thousands digit, a hundreds digit, a tens digit and a ones digit. The place tells you what the digit is worth. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand.

Partition

Partition 7,305 into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.

7 thousands = 7,000. 3 hundreds = 300. 0 tens = nothing. 5 ones = 5.

Answer: 7,000 + 300 + 5

1,000 more and 1,000 less

To find 1,000 more or 1,000 less, change only the thousands digit. The hundreds, tens and ones stay the same.

1,000 lessNumber1,000 more
3,3524,3525,352
2361,2362,236
7,9058,9059,905

Counting in 6s, 7s, 9s, 25s and 1,000s

Count inNumbers
6s6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60
7s7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70
9s9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72, 81, 90
25s25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150, 175, 200
1,000s2,405, 3,405, 4,405, 5,405, 6,405

Counting in 9s: add 10, then take away 1 (36 → 46 → 45). Counting in 25s always ends in 00, 25, 50 or 75.

Compare and order

First count the digits: a 4-digit number is greater than any 3-digit number. If both have 4 digits, compare place by place from the left until two digits are different.

Compare

6,089 ☐ 6,098

Thousands: 6 = 6. Hundreds: 0 = 0. Tens: 8 < 9.

Answer: 6,089 < 6,098

Estimate on a number line

Counting back through zero

Numbers below 0 are negative numbers. We write them with a minus sign: −1, −2, −3. We use them for temperatures below 0 °C.

Temperature

It is 3 °C. The temperature falls by 5 degrees. What is it now?

Count down 5: 2, 1, 0, −1, −2.

Answer: −2 °C

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Giving the digit, not its value (the 3 in 4,352 is 3)The 3 is in the hundreds place: 300
Leaving out a zero (4,000 + 60 + 2 = 462)Write 0 in the empty hundreds place: 4,062
Changing the wrong digit (1,000 more than 4,352 = 4,452)Change the thousands digit: 5,352
Comparing the first digits only (998 > 1,089)Count the digits first: 1,089 > 998
Skipping 0 when counting back (1, −1, −2)Say 0: 1, 0, −1

faq.q: What place value should a Year 4 child know?
faq.a: In Year 4 children work with numbers beyond 1,000. They know the value of each digit in a 4-digit number, find 1,000 more or less, count in 6s, 7s, 9s, 25s and 1,000s, compare and order numbers, and count back through zero.

faq.q: How do you find 1,000 more or less than a number?
faq.a: Change only the thousands digit by 1 and keep the other digits the same. 1,000 more than 4,352 is 5,352, and 1,000 less is 3,352.
Place value counters are round counters marked 1, 10, 100 or 1,000. Children build a number with them, for example 3 thousands, 4 tens and 2 ones make 3,042.

faq.q: Do Year 4 children learn negative numbers?
faq.a: Yes. The National Curriculum asks Year 4 pupils to count backwards through zero to include negative numbers, often on a number line or a thermometer, for example 2, 1, 0, −1, −2.

sets.title: Value of each digit in a 4-digit number

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 6 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 6 thousands = 6,000. The digit is 6, but its value is 6,000.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?

items.q: In 6,803, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 6,803 has 6 thousands, 8 hundreds, 0 tens, 3 ones. The hundreds digit is 8.

items.q: In 5,280, which digit is in the tens place?
items.e: 5,280 has 5 thousands, 2 hundreds, 8 tens, 0 ones. The tens digit is 8.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit?
items.e: The red 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 9,847?
items.e: The 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 6,987?
items.e: The 8 is in the tens place, so it is worth 8 tens = 80. The digit is 8, but its value is 80.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 9,467?
items.e: The 9 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 9 thousands = 9,000. The digit is 9, but its value is 9,000.

items.q: In 2,091, which digit is in the thousands place?
items.e: 2,091 has 2 thousands, 0 hundreds, 9 tens, 1 one. The thousands digit is 2.

items.q: In 3,518, which digit is in the hundreds place?
items.e: 3,518 has 3 thousands, 5 hundreds, 1 ten, 8 ones. The hundreds digit is 5.

items.q: In 2,543, what does the digit 5 stand for?
items.e: Read the places from the left: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones. The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it stands for 5 hundreds, or 500.

items.q: In 9,387, what does the digit 8 stand for?
items.e: Read the places from the left: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones. The 8 is in the tens place, so it stands for 8 tens, or 80.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 2,815?
items.e: The 8 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 8 hundreds = 800. The digit is 8, but its value is 800.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 7,543?
items.e: The 4 is in the tens place, so it is worth 4 tens = 40. The digit is 4, but its value is 40.

items.q: In 8,514, what does the digit 5 stand for?
items.e: Read the places from the left: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones. The 5 is in the hundreds place, so it stands for 5 hundreds, or 500.

items.q: Which number has a 7 in the hundreds place?
items.e: The hundreds place is the 3rd digit from the right. In 3,796 the 7 is there, so it is worth 700.

items.q: Which number has a 4 in the tens place?
items.e: The tens place is the 2nd digit from the right. In 5,246 the 4 is there, so it is worth 40.

items.q: Which number has a 5 in the thousands place?
items.e: The thousands place is the 4th digit from the right. In 5,638 the 5 is there, so it is worth 5,000.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count each kind of counter: 9 thousands, 8 hundreds, 5 tens, 2 ones. Write the digits in order: 9,852.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count each kind of counter: 3 thousands, 5 hundreds, 0 tens, 5 ones. Write the digits in order: 3,505. There are no tens, so write 0 in that place.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count each kind of counter: 4 thousands, 5 hundreds, 9 tens, 6 ones. Write the digits in order: 4,596.

items.q: What number is 9,000 + 800 + 8?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 9,000 + 800 + 8 = 9,808.

items.q: What number is 9,000 + 20 + 5?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 9,000 + 20 + 5 = 9,025.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count each kind of counter: 2 thousands, 1 hundred, 0 tens, 4 ones. Write the digits in order: 2,104. There are no tens, so write 0 in that place.

items.q: What number do the place value counters show?
items.e: Count each kind of counter: 6 thousands, 7 hundreds, 3 tens, 2 ones. Write the digits in order: 6,732.

items.q: Which shows 9,906 partitioned into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 9,000 + 900 + 6. A zero adds nothing, so it does not get its own part.

items.q: Which shows 8,069 partitioned into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 8,000 + 60 + 9. A zero adds nothing, so it does not get its own part.

items.q: 8,000 + ☐ + 40 + 3 = 8,543. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 8,543 has 5 in the hundreds place. 5 hundreds = 500, so the missing part is 500.

items.q: 8,000 + 100 + ☐ + 9 = 8,159. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 8,159 has 5 in the tens place. 5 tens = 50, so the missing part is 50.

items.q: ☐ + 700 + 60 + 3 = 1,763. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 1,763 has 1 in the thousands place. 1 thousand = 1,000, so the missing part is 1,000.

items.q: What number is 8,000 + 200 + 10?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 8,000 + 200 + 10 = 8,210.

items.q: What number is 9,000 + 100 + 6?
items.e: Put each digit in its place and write 0 in any empty place: 9,000 + 100 + 6 = 9,106.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: Each small mark is 1,000. The arrow is between 2,000 and 3,000, closer to 3,000. So it shows about 2,800.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: Each small mark is 1,000. The arrow is between 6,000 and 7,000, closer to 6,000. So it shows about 6,300.

items.q: Which shows 2,150 partitioned into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 2,000 + 100 + 50. A zero adds nothing, so it does not get its own part.

items.q: Which shows 3,027 partitioned into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones?
items.e: Write the value of each digit that is not 0: 3,000 + 20 + 7. A zero adds nothing, so it does not get its own part.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 3,000 to 4,000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100, not 10. The arrow is 7 marks after 3,000: 3,000 + 700 = 3,700.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 8,000 to 9,000 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 100, not 10. The arrow is 4 marks after 8,000: 8,000 + 400 = 8,400.

sets.title: 1,000 more or less and counting in 6s, 7s, 9s, 25s and 1,000s

items.q: What is 1,000 more than 4,352?
items.e: Only the thousands digit changes: 4 thousands → 5 thousands. The hundreds, tens and ones stay the same. 4,352 + 1,000 = 5,352.

items.q: What is 1,000 less than 7,068?
items.e: Only the thousands digit changes: 7 thousands → 6 thousands. The hundreds, tens and ones stay the same. 7,068 − 1,000 = 6,068.

items.q: What is 1,000 more than 2,097?
items.e: Only the thousands digit changes: 2 thousands → 3 thousands. The hundreds, tens and ones stay the same. 2,097 + 1,000 = 3,097.

items.q: What is 1,000 less than 1,236?
items.e: 1,236 has 1 thousand. Take it away and the thousands digit becomes 0: 1,236 − 1,000 = 236.

items.q: What is 1,000 more than 8,905?
items.e: Only the thousands digit changes: 8 thousands → 9 thousands. The hundreds, tens and ones stay the same. 8,905 + 1,000 = 9,905.

items.q: What is 1,000 less than 3,004?
items.e: Only the thousands digit changes: 3 thousands → 2 thousands. The hundreds, tens and ones stay the same. 3,004 − 1,000 = 2,004.

items.q: Count in 6s: 18, 24, 30, 36, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 6 more than the one before. 36 + 6 = 42.

items.q: Count in 7s: 35, 42, 49, 56, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 7 more than the one before. 56 + 7 = 63.

items.q: Count in 9s: 27, 36, 45, 54, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 9 more than the one before. 54 + 9 = 63.

items.q: Count in 25s: 125, 150, 175, 200, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 more than the one before. 200 + 25 = 225.
Each number is 1,000 more than the one before. 5,405 + 1,000 = 6,405. Only the thousands digit changes.

items.q: Which number would you say when counting in 9s from 0?
items.e: 7 × 9 = 63. 59 ends in 9 but is not in the 9 times table; 56 is 7 × 8 and 66 is 11 × 6.

items.q: Which number would you say when counting in 7s from 0?
items.e: 7 × 7 = 49. 47 ends in 7 but is not in the 7 times table; 54 is 6 × 9 and 36 is 6 × 6.

items.q: 1,000 more than a number is 6,281. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 1,000 more than the number is 6,281, the number is 1,000 less than 6,281: 5,281.

items.q: 1,000 less than a number is 3,940. What is the number?
items.e: Work backwards. If 1,000 less than the number is 3,940, the number is 1,000 more than 3,940: 4,940.

items.q: Count in 6s: 42, 48, ☐, 60, 66. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The numbers go up by 6 each time. 48 + 6 = 54. Check: 54 + 6 = 60.

items.q: Count back in 7s: 84, 77, 70, 63, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 7 less than the one before. 63 − 7 = 56.

items.q: Count back in 25s: 300, 275, 250, 225, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 25 less than the one before. 225 − 25 = 200.

items.q: Count back in 1,000s: 9,060, 8,060, 7,060, 6,060, ? What comes next?
items.e: Each number is 1,000 less than the one before. 6,060 − 1,000 = 5,060. Only the thousands digit changes.

items.q: Which number would you say when counting in 25s from 0?
items.e: Counting in 25s always ends in 00, 25, 50 or 75: 150, 175, 200. 155 and 205 end in 5 but are not multiples of 25.

sets.title: Compare and order numbers, and count back through zero

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 5 tens is more than 2 tens. So 4,352 > 4,325.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 9 tens is more than 8 tens. So 6,098 > 6,089.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 1,023 has 4 digits and 987 has only 3, so 1,023 is greater. A bigger first digit (9) does not matter when there are fewer digits.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 1 ten is more than 0 tens. So 5,710 > 5,701.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 7 hundreds is more than 2 hundreds. So 4,712 > 4,271. 4,712 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 9 hundreds is more than 8 hundreds. So 4,958 > 4,895. 4,958 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: 998 has only 3 digits, so it is the smallest, even though 9 is a big digit. Of the 4-digit numbers, compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 9 tens is more than 8 tens. So 1,098 > 1,089. 1,098 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the hundreds place: 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds. So 7,549 > 7,459. 7,459 is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: Compare from the left. The digits are the same until the tens place: 8 tens is more than 6 tens. So 3,186 > 3,168. 3,168 is the smallest.

items.q: Which number is the smallest?
items.e: 1,026 has 4 digits and 999 has only 3, so 1,026 is greater. 999 is the smallest.

items.q: Put 9,814, 9,481, 9,418 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 9,418 < 9,481 (tens: 1 < 8). 9,481 < 9,814 (hundreds: 4 < 8). So the order is 9,418, 9,481, 9,814.

items.q: Put 2,157, 2,751, 2,517 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare from the left. 2,157 < 2,517 (hundreds: 1 < 5). 2,517 < 2,751 (hundreds: 5 < 7). So the order is 2,157, 2,517, 2,751.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. Count back from 0: −1, −2, −3. The answer is −3.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. It is 2 marks past −5: count −6, −7. The answer is −7.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: The arrow is to the left of 0, so the number is negative. Count back from 0: −1, −2, −3, −4. The answer is −4.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: The red line ends below 0, so the temperature is negative. Each mark is 1 degree. Count down from 0: −1, −2, −3, −4, −5, −6. It shows −6 °C.

items.q: What temperature does the thermometer show?
items.e: The red line ends below 0, so the temperature is negative. Each mark is 1 degree. Count down from 0: −1, −2. It shows −2 °C.

items.q: Count back in 3s: 7, 4, 1, ? What comes next?
items.e: Count back 3 from 1, one at a time: 0, −1, −2. Remember to count 0. The answer is −2.

items.q: Count back in 10s: 30, 20, 10, 0, ? What comes next?
items.e: 10 less than 0 is 10 below zero, so it is −10. Do not forget the minus sign: 10 is above zero.

items.q: Count back in 2s: 5, 3, 1, ? What comes next?
items.e: Count back 2 from 1, one at a time: 0, −1. Remember to count 0. The answer is −1.

items.q: A football stadium has 4,068 seats. What is the value of the digit 6 in 4,068?
items.e: The 6 is in the tens place, so it is worth 6 tens = 60.

items.q: There are 7 days in a week. How many days are there in 8 weeks?
items.e: Count in 7s eight times: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56. 8 × 7 = 56 days.

items.q: Eggs come in boxes of 6. How many eggs are in 9 boxes?
Freya counts on in 1,000s from 2,450: 2,450, 3,450, … What is the 5th number she says?
items.e: Write the 5 numbers: 2,450, 3,450, 4,450, 5,450, 6,450. The 5th number is 6,450.

items.q: Four friends counted their steps on a school trip. Isla: 6,240; Kai: 6,420; Maya: 6,204; Evie: 6,402. Who walked the most steps?
items.e: All four numbers have 6 thousands. Compare the hundreds: 6,420 and 6,402 have 4 hundreds. Then the tens: 2 tens > 0 tens, so 6,420 is the greatest. Kai walked the most.

items.q: A shop has 4 boxes of 1,000 stickers, 12 packs of 100 stickers and 6 single stickers. How many stickers is that?
items.e: 12 hundreds = 1 thousand and 2 hundreds. So there are 5 thousands, 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones: 4,000 + 1,200 + 6 = 5,206.

items.q: The village of Ashby has 2,507 people. Which shows 2,507 partitioned?
items.e: 2,507 has 2 thousands, 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones: 2,000 + 500 + 7. The 0 tens adds nothing.

items.q: Last year 5,083 people visited a castle. This year 1,000 fewer people visited. How many people visited this year?
items.e: 1,000 fewer: only the thousands digit changes. 5 thousands → 4 thousands. 5,083 − 1,000 = 4,083.

items.q: Ava thinks of a number. It has 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 8 tens and 6 ones. What is her number?
items.e: Write the digits in order: 3 thousands, 0 hundreds, 8 tens, 6 ones → 3,086. The 0 keeps the 3 in the thousands place.

items.q: Jack's family parks in a car park. The ground floor is level 0. The floors below ground are level −1, level −2 and so on. He gets into the lift on level 2 and goes down 4 levels. Which level is he on now?
items.e: Count down 4 from level 2: 1, 0, −1, −2. Do not skip level 0. He is on level −2.

items.q: Use each of the digits 3, 8, 0 and 5 once to make the greatest 4-digit number.
items.e: Put the biggest digit in the thousands place, then the next biggest, and so on: 8, 5, 3, 0. The greatest number is 8,530.

items.q: Each bench in the school hall seats 9 children. How many children can sit on 7 benches?
items.e: Count in 9s seven times: 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63. 7 × 9 = 63 children.

items.q: Three secondary schools have 1,253, 1,325, 1,235 pupils. Which list shows these numbers from smallest to greatest?
items.e: All have 1 thousand. 1,235 and 1,253 have 2 hundreds, 1,325 has 3 hundreds. 1,235 < 1,253 because 3 tens < 5 tens. Order: 1,235, 1,253, 1,325.

items.q: In the evening the temperature was 3 °C. During the night it fell by 5 degrees. What was the temperature then?
items.e: Fell means count down. From 3 count down 5: 2, 1, 0, −1, −2. Do not skip 0. It was −2 °C.

items.q: Ethan's step goal is 10,000 steps a day. The arrow shows how many steps he has walked so far today. About how many steps is that?
items.e: Each mark is 1,000 steps. The arrow is halfway between 7,000 and 8,000, so it shows about 7,500 steps.

items.q: These villages have these populations: Westbrook 1,064; Little Ashby 1,406; Millford 1,460; Oakley 1,046. Which village has the smallest population?
items.e: All four have 1 thousand. 1,064 and 1,046 have 0 hundreds. Compare the tens: 4 tens < 6 tens, so 1,046 is the smallest. Oakley has the smallest population.

items.q: The caretaker stacks chairs in piles of 25. How many chairs are in 6 piles?
items.e: Count in 25s six times: 25, 50, 75, 100, 125, 150. There are 150 chairs.

items.q: Poppy's dad is a lorry driver. He has driven 3,950 km this month. Next month he will drive 1,000 km more than this. How far will he drive next month?
items.e: 1,000 more: only the thousands digit changes. 3 thousands → 4 thousands. 3,950 + 1,000 = 4,950 km.

items.q: At 7:00 am the temperature was −3 °C. By lunchtime it was 4 degrees warmer. What was the temperature at lunchtime?
items.e: Warmer means count up. From −3 °C count up 4: −2, −1, 0, 1. Do not skip 0. It was 1 °C.

items.q: One winter morning the temperatures were: Edinburgh −4 °C; Belfast −1 °C; Cardiff 2 °C; Manchester −2 °C. Which city was the coldest?
items.e: The coldest temperature is the one furthest below 0. −4 °C is 4 degrees below 0, which is colder than −2 °C or −1 °C. Edinburgh was the coldest.
